requiredFindings.title: Latch snapshot read failures before returning them from the sender
requiredFindings.description: The source.read error is converted with map_err and propagated without self.refuse. send_next likewise propagates realize_next failures without latching them. After Hello, OpenUniverse and SnapshotManifest, a transient read error on the first chunk therefore returns Source while refused remains false and the cursor, sequence and slot still identify that chunk. Restoring the source lets send_next resume successfully; cancel can also succeed after the failure. This contradicts the published Source/refusal contract that every such failure ends the transcript. The participant separately latches host_fault, but the public Ts2Sender API does not. The failed-source case at the end of every_divergence_refuses_before_writing asserts only the first error and omits ended(), unlike its other cases.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Make snapshot read errors irreversibly close the sender transcript before returning Source, including when realize_next is called directly. Audit the public sender failure exits for the same omission, including cancel-before-Hello through cancel(), and preserve the accepted prefix.
requiredFindings.validationExpectation: At the first chunk, inject a source I/O error, restore the source, and assert next_slot is None, cancel_payload is None, and realize_next/send_next/admit/cancel/admit_cancel refuse AfterRefusal without another source read or accepted frame. Cover a failure after an earlier chunk as well as at the first chunk; extend the failed-source test with the same ended-transcript assertions used for divergences.
